transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been feeling a little off my usual game lately? It's really nothing too terrible, I promise. It's just that the things that usually make me feel like myself—like my weekend photography walks, mentoring the kids, or even just keeping a perfectly clean calendar at work—they've started feeling sort of... flat. And heavy, I guess. I've just sort of stopped initiating them. 

I feel a little embarrassed even admitting that, because I'm usually so reliable and I really don't want to come across as lazy or anything. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um, let me think... I suppose it's been about a year and three months? Give or take a little. It kind of started right after... well, a family member of mine had some unexpected changes in their health. And their behavior, too. So I stepped in and took on a lot more of the coordination for them. 

I really don't mind helping out, I promise. I do that sort of organizing all day at work anyway, so it just made sense for me to handle it. I guess maybe juggling all that extra responsibility just sort of caught up with me eventually? I hope it's okay to admit that. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about being there for my family... is it normal to feel a little drained after taking on something like that?
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like your photography walks or mentoring?

Well, um... I guess so? I mean, I wouldn't say I've lost *all* interest. I still think photography is wonderful, and the kids in the mentoring program are just great. It's just... 

I suppose I haven't actually gone on a photo walk in a little while. And I might have missed a few mentoring sessions recently. But it's not that I don't like doing them anymore! It's just that I've been so busy with everything else, you know? The family stuff and work. Sometimes at the end of the day, I just... I don't quite have the energy to get out the door again. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm giving up on my hobbies or the kids. I really do intend to get back to them as soon as things settle down a bit. Do you think it's understandable to take a little break from those things when life gets busy?
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, even when there’s nothing specific going wrong?

Oh, um... no, I really wouldn't say I feel depressed. I mean, I definitely don't sit around feeling sad all day or anything like that. 

Like I was saying, it's more just... a lack of energy, I guess? I always try to keep a really positive attitude. You know, at work, you kind of have to be the upbeat one who keeps the office running smoothly, so I always make sure to keep a smile on for everyone. I really try my best not to let myself get into a slump. 

So, no, I don't feel down most of the day. I hope that's a good sign? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, walking around crying or feeling sorry for myself. I really do try to stay as cheerful as I can.
Have you been feeling fatigued or experiencing a loss of energy nearly every day, even when you haven't been particularly busy?

Well, um... no, I definitely wouldn't say that. If I actually get a quiet day—which, you know, doesn't happen too often lately!—I feel perfectly fine. 

It's really just the heavy workload that wears me out a little bit. If I haven't been busy, I have plenty of energy to get things done around the house or whatever else needs doing. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm just, you know, sitting around feeling lethargic when there's nothing on my plate. I always try to stay as productive as I can. 

That's pretty normal, isn't it? To only feel tired when you've actually been working hard?
